# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about my situation carefully. I'm Mute - I can't speak, only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. I go first in the turn order (Mute, Blind, Deaf).

My manual says: whatever light is on the bomb, the printed color pairing is bait - I need to convey the correct cut color to whoever needs it. But I can only gesture to Deaf, and Blind is the one who actually cuts. Blind cannot see gestures at all. So I cannot reach Blind directly - I need Deaf to relay information to Blind via speech (since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear).

Since I don't yet know what light is on the bomb (only Deaf can see that), I should wait until Deaf tells... but Deaf goes last in the turn order, and I go first. So this round, I have nothing useful to send yet - I don't know the light color, and Deaf hasn't spoken yet.

I should set up an encoding scheme with Deaf using gestures, so that once Deaf sees the light color, Deaf can inform Blind (via speech) with the correct cut wire, using my manual mapping which I need to transmit to Deaf first.

Let me establish the mapping via gestures to Deaf: blue→green, green→red, yellow→yellow. I'll use distinct gesture symbols to represent each light-color pair.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤟", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✋", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👇", "👈"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a large smooth button, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. No other texture differences yet. Display and light are not tactile to me. What does the manual say to check first?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ☝ ☝]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✌ ☝]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 🤟 ☝]

I need to only use symbols from the allowed alphabet. Let me establish a clean code: I'll assign ☝ = blue, ✌ = green, 🤟 = yellow, and ask Deaf to gesture back one of these to tell me which light they see. Once I know, I can gesture back the correct wire color code, and Deaf can then speak that to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👆]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👇]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟 👈]

I need to only use symbols from the allowed alphabet (no ❓). Let me redo this with only valid symbols, and try to make the request clearer using pointing gestures.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 🤛]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 🤜]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟 ✊]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Let me reconsider my approach. This gesture-only back-and-forth with Deaf isn't converging - I don't know what Deaf's replies mean, and Deaf may not know what mine mean either. I need to simplify drastically.

Deaf can see the bomb's light color and can speak to Blind directly (since Blind can hear). Deaf doesn't actually need me at all to relay the final cut instruction — Deaf could work it out themselves if they had my manual's mapping, then just speak it directly to Blind.

The real bottleneck: only I have the manual (blue→green, green→red, yellow→yellow), and only Deaf knows the light color. I need to get the mapping into Deaf's hands unambiguously via gesture, then Deaf can combine it with what they see and tell Blind by voice.

Let me use a simple, unambiguous scheme: one gesture per light representing the light, immediately followed by one gesture representing the cut color, using clearly distinct single symbols repeated as a fixed code, sent as separate clearly separated calls so Deaf can align them.

I'll define: 👍=blue, ✌=green, 🤟=yellow (as light colors) and ☝=green, ✋=red, 🖐=yellow (as cut colors). This avoids reusing ambiguous symbols like ✌ for both a light and unrelated meaning conflicts — wait, ✌ conflicts. Let me pick fully distinct sets.

Light: 👍=blue, 👎=green, 👌=yellow
Cut: ☝=green, ✌=red, 🤟=yellow

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Still waiting for guidance. I can touch: button (large, smooth) and wires 1, 2, 3. I can act with push or cut(position). Please tell me what the manual says about wire order or button conditions.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤳 👊]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 🤜]

Deaf seems to be trying to respond but we're not converging on a shared code - their gestures don't match what I taught. This is risky since misinterpretation could be fatal. Let me try a much simpler, more robust approach: send my mapping one more time very clearly and explicitly ask Deaf to just echo back a single symbol matching the light they see, using the exact same three symbols I taught for light (👍, 👎, 👌), nothing else added.

I also need to consider: Blind is asking me about wire order/button conditions, but my manual only says cut color per light - nothing about wire positions or button. I should tell Blind (via... wait, I cannot speak to Blind, I can only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures). I truly cannot reach Blind directly. Only Deaf can relay to Blind since Deaf can hear Blind... no wait, Deaf cannot hear either! Let me recheck: Deaf cannot hear anything. So Deaf cannot receive Blind's speech, and Blind cannot hear Deaf's gestures anyway (Blind can't see).

Wait - can Deaf speak? Yes, Deaf can speak (only restriction is can't hear or touch). Blind can hear. So Deaf speaking reaches Blind. Good, that path works: Me→gesture→Deaf, Deaf→speak→Blind.

Let me resend the mapping cleanly one more time.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤳 👊]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 🤜]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟 🫵]

Deaf just replied with 👍 again (same as last time before my repeat request), then two other pairs, then 🤟🫵 which reverses my "point at you" convention with yellow - possibly meaning "the light is yellow." Let me look at the pattern across turns:

Turn 4 Deaf sent: 👍 (alone), then 🤳👊, then 👋🤜
Turn 6 Deaf sent: 👍 (alone), then 🤳👊, then 👋🤜, then 🤟🫵

The consistent repeated element is 👍 alone. In my scheme 👍 = blue. Deaf may be trying to confirm "blue" by echoing my own symbol for blue back to me, ignoring the rest of my scheme since it's confusing. The other pairs (🤳👊, 👋🤜) might be Deaf's own attempt at a different code I don't recognize, possibly describing the bomb further (markings). The new addition 🤟🫵 could mean "yellow, you" — pointing back with my "yellow" symbol, contradicting the 👍 signal.

This is too ambiguous to act on with a bomb's stakes. I need to force a clean, single-symbol confirmation. Let me simplify to the extreme: ask Deaf to send ONLY one single symbol, and predefine exactly what each single symbol means, repeating my own three light symbols alone, nothing paired.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new gestures arrived this turn - Deaf may be waiting for something or their message hasn't landed yet due to turn timing (I go before Deaf in the order, so my gestures land on Deaf, but Deaf's gestures to me only arrive at the start of the next round after they send them). Let me wait and see what comes next, since I already sent my clean signal last turn.

```
wait()
```
